text:
ashwin: Heads up — p95 latency on inter-GPU RPCs jumped to ~450ms during the 11:50-12:05 batching window on eu-west-1; seen across three racks :warning:
ops-bot: [ALERT] cluster/eu-west-1/interconnect p95 spike at 2026-03-18T11:51:12Z (rule: interconnect-p95>200ms)
jeff: I see it on the dashboard — all models show token streaming stalls, CPU OK, GPUs busy. Link: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/infra/interconnect?from=now-2h&to=now
kai: grabbing tcpdumps from a few nodes in rack-18 and rack-21 now. Running: sudo tcpdump -i bond0 -w /tmp/ew-spike-r18.pcap 'tcp and port 1024'
maria: did we get any RDMA timeouts in dmesg? last time RDMA timeout correlated with tx retries/queue stalls.
linda: checked on one affected host: dmesg shows a repeated mlx5_core error around the spike: 
```
[15234.112345] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: qpair 42 retry timeout
[15234.112347] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: async event: qp timeout
[15234.112350] RQ overflow detected on mlx5_0
```
ashwin: that lines up with what I saw in the infra metrics: mlx5 tx_retries spiked from 0 to ~120 in 30s.
jeff: did we push any NIC firmware or kernel updates in the last 24h?
kai: no kernel rollouts this morning; we did roll a NIC FW on a small subset two nights ago in ap-south, not eu-west. Checking ethtool and ibv: 
```
ethtool -S ens5f0 | grep tx_
  tx_packets: 123456
  tx_dropped: 0
ibstat -l
  mlx5_0: ports: 1 2
```
maria: MTU mismatch? I know fragmentation + offload can trigger fallback and cause tx path stalls. Can someone paste ip link show on affected nodes?
linda: one affected node: ip link show bond0 mtu 9000 qlen 1000
other node in same rack: ip link show bond0 mtu 1500 qlen 1000
ashwin: aha — mixed MTU in the same east-west fabric. That would force fragmentation on some flows. But would that explain RDMA qp timeouts?
kai: maybe compounded — IP fragmentation triggers fallback and forces jumbo frames to be dropped, inflight RDMA flows hit retries; also saw increased TCP retransmits in the pcap. Extracted flows show repeated SACKs and retransmits.
jeff: timeline: autoscaler moved some nodes during maintenance, those nodes came up with default MTU 1500 while rack generally uses 9000. Could be a provisioning bug in the node bootstrap.
sre-oncall: remediation plan? We need quick mitigation to stop customer impact.
maria: two options: 1) adjust batch window temporarily — reduce max_batch_size to lower east-west load (app-level); 2) force MTU to 9000 on nodes that are mis-configured and drain gracefully; 3) enable TCP fallback with lower batch concurrency for affected racks.
linda: I can push a config change to the node bootstrap but that won't be immediate. I can run sudo ip link set dev bond0 mtu 9000 on the two affected hosts now if ops approves.
ashwin: proceed with direct MTU fix on 2 nodes in rack-21, mark them unsched, do one at a time. If that reduces tx_retries we can roll to the rest.
ops-bot: deploy request queued: change mtu on i-0a1,batchhost-21a and i-0b2,batchhost-21b — approval needed from @sre-oncall
sre-oncall: approved, do one host at a time and monitor p95 for 5 minutes between changes.
kai: starting live capture on both; doing first host now. Running: sudo ip link set dev bond0 mtu 9000 && systemctl restart network-service
(later) kai: after MTU fix on batchhost-21a p95 dropped from 450ms -> 120ms within 90s. tx_retries back to baseline.
jeff: awesome. That looks like the main offender. Any reason others are still spiking?
linda: rack-18 still shows intermittent spikes — checking for other mismatches or partial MTU changes in transit ToR. Could be a ToR config or firmware that reset.
maria: also check ECMP next-hop churn. If some ToRs advertise different path MTU or have asymmetric path causing fragmentation on return, packets can get dropped.
kai: pulled SNMP and switch logs from tor-18: shows a brief interface reset on sw-tor-18-2 at 11:50:08, likely during a flapping event. Might have briefly negotiated a fallback to 1500.
ashwin: root cause hypothesis: a mixture of node bootstrap MTU mismatches + a transient ToR interface reset during peak batching window triggered packet fragmentation and RDMA qp retries, causing p95 spikes.
jeff: next actions: 
- lind a: add a bootstrap check to ensure mtu=9000 on all GPU node provisioning templates (PR in infra-config)
- kai: create a short alert for MTU drift per rack (if any node mtu != expected)
- maria: add an RDMA retry SLO alert so we can catch qp retry spikes before customer p95 rises
- ops: run a one-off scan for nodes with mtu!=9000 in eu-west-1 and fix asap
ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-7342: "eu-west-1 MTU drift and ToR flaps causing inter-node latency spikes" with links to pcaps and dmesg.
sre-oncall: assign to eng-infra oncall and infra-boot team — follow-up retro tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
linda: rolling mtu fixes to 6 more affected nodes now, doing one-per-rack to avoid blips.
kai: capture summary attached in the ticket: tcpdump pcap + extracted tcp retransmit counts + dmesg excerpt.
ashwin: thanks all. If anyone sees a reappearance ping me. For now fallback rule: if cluster interconnect p95 > 200ms during batch window, reduce batch concurrency by 30% automatically to avoid cascading GPU queueing costs.
jeff: logging cost note — these retries increased token-cost by ~6% during the 15m window because models retried and some requests timed out, filing cost impact estimate in INFRA-7342.
maria: retro items: tighten provisioning tests (MTU, QPs), add ToR SW health monitor, and test RDMA failover behavior in staging with mixed MTU to ensure graceful degradation.
ashwin: closing thread — good catch, quick fix, follow-ups in ticket. :thumbsup:
